transcript: Tonight I attended the opening of The Sign in Sydney brewstein's Window on Broadway, fresh off of its production at BAM earlier this year. In the play, Sydney is living in New York with his wife Iris, and much of the story looks at their struggles in their personal lives, certainly in their marriage, but also individually in terms of identity and in a broader sense of understanding the world, society and life in general. Other characters come in and out that help illuminate some of these themes, talk about politics, homophobia, racism and other isms, and overall the plays about friction and dissonance, friction between detaching from conventions in order to self preserve and earnestly searching for meaning, friction between cynicism and hope. But despite this broad scope and the big abstract conversations and debates the characters get into, I thought the writing was incredibly profound, nuanced and realistic. I thought Oscar Isaac as Sydney really embodied this genuine yearning to understand the world with good intentions while simultaneously displaying blind spots, a sense of intellectual superiority and hypocrisy. In some ways, this is a play about our imperfections, and it demands us to see them. And in some ways, we're all like Sydney. This play gets 2 thumbs up for me with that. Another playbill for my collection.
